messages.body_plain:
Hi list,

Is there a way to have knitr still generate figures, but not print them in the document?  If not, how about making this an option from fig.show?

The use case I imagine is the following.  I'm writing a manuscript for a journal with wonderfully archaic but common policies: they will not take pdf format (they don't say what they *will* take), they will only take eps graphics and do not want them included in the text.  With the option above, it seems like it would be easy to generate the format they require automatically when necessary (knitr + pandoc + Makefile).

(Or maybe externalization of the figures can be done with pandoc after knitr makes output markdown?)

-Carl

messages.body_plain:
If you want to exclude the whole chunk output (including figures), you
can simply use include=FALSE; all results are still generated by not
included.

If you only want to exclude figures in particular, it is also easy --
reset the plot hook so that plots are not included, e.g.

knit_hooks$set(plot = function(x, options) "")  # insert empty strings for plots

other types of results will remain there.

#!/usr/bin/env Rscript

local({

  insert_line_numbers <- function(tex_file,  By = 5){
  require(stringr)
  doc <- readLines(tex_file)
  code_lines   <- grep("^(\\\\hlstd|\\\\hlfunctioncall)", doc)
  max_lines    <- length(code_lines)
  line_numbers <- rep('', max_lines)
  line_numbers[c(1, seq(5, max_lines,  by=By))] <- c('1', seq(5, max_lines,  by=By))
  line_numbers <- str_pad(line_numbers, nchar(line_numbers[max_lines])+1)
  ## line_numbers <- str_pad(seq_along(code_lines), width = 2, side = "left")
  ## line_numbers <- str_c("\\1\\\\hlline\\{", line_numbers, "   \\}\\2")
  line_numbers <- str_c("\\\\hlline\\{\\\\llap\\{", line_numbers, "   \\\\quad\\}\\}\\1\\2")

  pat <- "^(\\\\hlstd\\{\\}|\\\\hlfunctioncall\\{.*\\})(.*)$"
  doc[code_lines] <- str_replace(doc[code_lines], pat, line_numbers)
  writeLines(doc, tex_file)
##  return(path.expand(tex_file))
}

  p = commandArgs(TRUE)
    if (length(p) == 0L || '--help' %in% p) {

    library(knitr)
  knit_fun = if ('--pdf' %in% p) {
    p = setdiff(p, '--pdf')
    if (length(p) == 0L) stop('no input file provided')
    knit2pdf
  } else knit

  if (!file.exists(p[1]))
    stop("file '", p[1], "' does not exist!")

  lineno <- FALSE

    lineno <- TRUE
    p = setdiff(p, '--lineno')
  }

<<>>=

<<foo-plot, eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE>>=
par(mar=c(4, 4, .1, .1))

@

messages.body_plain:
Hi baptiste,

This is probably not as obvious as other hooks, since I did not export
the function to highlight source code. Anyway, it is certainly
possible because the inline hook has access to the code in \Sexpr{}.
Here is a quick experiment (note I quoted read.table() so that it is a
character string otherwise it will be an R expression to be evaluated;
you may need to try() highlighting because not all results are valid R
code):

\documentclass{article}
<<setup, include=FALSE>>=
knit_hooks$set(inline = function(x) {
  if (is.numeric(x)) return(knitr:::format_sci(x, 'latex'))
  x = as.character(x)
  knitr:::hilight_source(x, 'latex', list(prompt=FALSE, size='normalsize'))
})
@
\begin{document}

the value of $\pi$ is \Sexpr{pi}, and the function to read a table is
\Sexpr{'read.table()'}.

<<test2>>=
rnorm(10)
@
\end{document}

Regards,
Yihui

Dear list,

(Apologies for being borderline off-topic)
I'm making a presentation in Beamer using knitr and xetex; I'm usually
happy with Inconsolata as a fixed width font for code chunks but I
noticed that some symbols, $ and <- in particular, can look quite ugly
because they have a wrong size / kerning in the context of R code. Do
you know a trick to special-case and fine-tune such characters? The
listing package can do some automatic replacements such as <- becoming
an arrow but I wonder if i) I can still use syntax highlighting based
on the parser, ii) copy+paste can work with such characters?

Thanks,

baptiste

I think the relevant piece should be this:

\setbox\hlnormalsizeboxlessthan=\hbox{\begin{normalsize}\verb.<.\end{normalsize}}%
\setbox\hlnormalsizeboxdollar=\hbox{\begin{normalsize}\verb.$.\end{normalsize}}%

that is where <- and $ are defined by the highlight package. I'm not
familiar with \setbox, but I guess there might be a way like
\renewcommand to redefine these symbols... Another nasty trick is to
customize the 'source' hook; see render_latex (I replaced " with "{}
there, and you can also do other jobs there).

For listings, unfortunately you cannot copy the arrow, but you can
customize the definitions so that <- is not turned to a real arrow.

work with than the fragile LaTeX:
